title: Goals and systems
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: Do you chase the result, or build the process that makes it?

Jose said the call would add material beyond the book for those who had already read it, and that it is collaborative, not like a school: veterans and young entrepreneurs, each giving their perspective.
A student said: goals are about the results you want to achieve. Systems are about the process that leads to those results.
Jose said that he uses the word systems a lot, because when you systemize things you make your time more efficient, and when you make your time more efficient you have more free time.
He said that you leverage other people's time: if you are not doing the job, somebody has to. You give them a job description, and then you have to audit the process.
He said auditing can be anywhere from one to ten. At a one, you don't know what is going on and you rely blindly on the person's charisma. He wants to audit every little thing until it is granular.
He used the metaphor of a car going around a track: some people know the engine, the suspension, the tires. You have to be fluent enough at auditing to hear which part makes the noise.
He said that when he arrives somewhere, he wants everything he has to look at to take ten minutes or less, so that he is checking a list, not training someone all over again.

He said that systems lead to patterns in our daily living, and patterns help us discover opportunities: what am I doing today to seize them? He said that if you have only one fishing line in the water, the chances are a fish will not hit it, so put more lines in, and make sure someone is there to reel it in.
What is one process in your work that you could check in ten minutes?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the process that would produce it.
Write who you would hand part of it to.
Write how you would audit it in ten minutes.
Write how many lines you have in the water.

check.q: What did a student say systems are about?
choices: The process that leads to results

check.q: What did Jose say you do after you give someone a job description?
What did Jose say about one fishing line in the water?

recap: Build the process, not just the goal. Audit it granularly.
